 Key Points Regular service providers usually get the cost of one visit or about a week’s pay, while crews and occasional helpers get $10 to $50 each.
 USPS carriers and other federal workers can’t accept cash or cash-like gift cards, and their gifts top out at $20 per occasion.
 Bankrate found fewer Americans planned holiday tips in 2025, but the median tip held steady at $50 for house cleaners.
 Holiday tips are a thank-you to the people who show up for you all year, from the house cleaner to the crew that hauls your trash. The hard part is deciding who makes the list and how much fits your holiday budget .
 This chart covers 78 service providers, from nannies and doormen to dog walkers and delivery drivers. You’ll find a suggested amount for each one, the rules that limit what some workers can accept, and a planner that totals your list. Treat every amount as a starting point, and track the total in a budgeting app as you give.

 How Much Should You Tip For The Holidays In 2026?
 For anyone you see every week or two, a holiday tip equal to the cost of one visit is the standard. Full-time nannies and daily dog walkers usually get about a week’s pay, and crews you rarely see get $10 to $50 per person. These ranges track the Emily Post Institute’s holiday tipping advice , and you can fund them from a high-yield savings account you set up for holiday spending.
 $50 Median Tip For House Cleaners $50 Median Tip For Lawn And Snow Crews $25 Median Gift For Teachers $20 Median Gift For Mail Carriers Those medians come from Bankrate’s 2025 holiday tipping survey of 2,445 U.S. adults. They reflect what people actually give, which often lands below etiquette ranges. Check your list against your own emergency fund and cash flow before you commit.
 Holiday Tipping Rules Of Thumb
 Weekly Or Biweekly Service: The cost of one visit, such as one cleaning, one haircut, or one training session. Full-Time Caregivers: About one week’s pay for a nanny, au pair, or private caregiver, often with a small gift from the family. Crews And Routes: $10 to $50 per worker for trash, lawn, snow, and building staff you see now and then. Government Workers: A non-cash gift worth $20 or less, or a card, since many can’t take cash. Professionals: Doctors, lawyers, and accountants get a card or office treats, not cash. People You Tip Every Visit: A smaller holiday tip or a card is plenty. Adjust from there based on how often you use the service, how many years you’ve worked together, and where you live, since big-city tips run higher. If your list runs long, our ways to earn extra cash for Christmas can cover the difference.
 Holiday Tipping Chart For 2026: Who To Tip And How Much
 The chart below lists 78 people you might thank this season, grouped by where they show up in your life. Each amount is The College Investor’s suggested range, built from Emily Post Institute advice and Bankrate survey data, and you can scale any of them to fit the budget you set .
 In-Home Help: Nannies, Sitters, And House Cleaners
 People who work inside your home every week sit at the top of most lists, and they usually get the largest tips. Full-time childcare is also where tax rules kick in, and a dependent care FSA through work can help cover the regular cost of that care.
 Holiday Tips 2026 : In-Home Help Who Suggested Tip Or Gift Good To Know 
 House Cleaner (Weekly Or Biweekly) Cost of one visit Hand it over at the last visit before the holiday. 
 House Cleaner (Monthly Or Occasional) Half of one visit, or $20 to $50 Less frequent service earns a smaller thank-you. 
 Full-Time Nanny One week’s pay, plus a small gift from your child A cash bonus counts as wages for payroll tax. 
 Au Pair Or Live-In Nanny One to two weeks’ pay, plus a gift Check whether your au pair agency sets any rules. 
 Regular Babysitter One night’s pay, plus a small gift from your child Bump it up if they work most weekends. 
 Occasional Babysitter Gift card or treat, $20 to $30 A card from the kids makes it personal. 
 Personal Chef Or Meal Prep Cook Cost of one session Only for an ongoing arrangement. 
 Private Home Health Aide One week’s pay, or a gift Agency aides follow agency rules instead. 
 House Sitter $25 to $50, or a gift Most relevant if they cover your holiday travel. 
 Source: The College Investor, Emily Post Institute, Bankrate. Outdoor And Home Maintenance Crews
 Crews you rarely see in person still keep your home running, and a modest cash tip per worker is standard. Give each worker an envelope so the money reaches everyone, and plan the crew total in your holiday budget .
 Holiday Tips 2026 : Outdoor And Home Maintenance Crews Who Suggested Tip Or Gift Good To Know 
 Lawn And Garden Crew $20 to $50 per worker Bankrate’s 2025 median was $50. 
 Snow Removal Crew $20 to $50 per worker, or one visit Tip after the first big storm if you prefer. 
 Pool Cleaner Cost of one visit Year-round service only. 
 Regular Handyman $25 to $50, or a gift Skip it if you call them once a year. 
 Pest Control Technician $20 to $30, or snacks Only for a recurring technician. 
 Window Washer $20 to $30 Regular service only. 
 Gutter Or Chimney Crew No holiday tip needed One-time jobs get thanked at the time of service. 
 Source: The College Investor, Emily Post Institute, Bankrate. Kids, School, And Lessons
 Teachers and caregivers get gifts more often than cash, and school rules often set the limit. Private tutors and lesson teachers are different, since you pay them directly, and the average cost of tutoring gives you a baseline for one session.
 Holiday Tips 2026 : Kids, School, And Lessons Who Suggested Tip Or Gift Good To Know 
 Daycare Teacher $25 to $70 per teacher, or a gift Check the center’s policy first. 
 Preschool Teacher Gift card, $25 to $50 A class gift works well here. 
 K-12 Teacher Gift or gift card, about $25, or a class gift Public school rules can cap gifts. Bankrate’s 2025 median was $25. 
 Teacher’s Aide Or Paraprofessional Gift card, $15 to $25 Often forgotten and always appreciated. 
 School Bus Driver Gift card or treat, $15 to $25 District employees may face gift limits. 
 After-School Program Staff $20 to $40, or a group gift Pool with other families for a bigger thank-you. 
 Private Tutor Cost of one session Only for weekly sessions. 
 Music Or Lesson Teacher Cost of one lesson Swim, dance, and art teachers count too. 
 Youth Sports Coach Team gift, $10 to $20 per family Volunteer coaches love a group card. 
 College Professor A thank-you note, no gift Grading makes gifts awkward. 
 Source: The College Investor, Emily Post Institute, Bankrate. Apartment And Building Staff
 Building staff tips scale with your city and how much the staff does for you, and big-city doormen sit at the top of the range. If you rent, think of it like any other housing cost and plan it into your monthly budget ahead of December.
 Holiday Tips 2026 : Apartment And Building Staff Who Suggested Tip Or Gift Good To Know 
 Doorman $25 to $100 each Higher in big cities and full-service buildings. 
 Building Superintendent $50 to $150 More if they handle repairs for you often. 
 Maintenance Staff Or Porter $20 to $50 each Give to each person you see regularly. 
 Concierge Or Front Desk $20 to $50 each Ask if the building pools a holiday fund. 
 Parking Garage Attendant $20 to $50 For a monthly spot. 
 Security Guard $20 to $40 Contract guards may have employer rules. 
 HOA Or Property Manager A card or treats, no cash They’re salaried staff. 
 Source: The College Investor, Emily Post Institute, Bankrate. Mail, Packages, And Delivery
 Delivery is the category with the most rules, because federal law and company policies limit what drivers can accept. Gig drivers on apps like DoorDash and Instacart are the easy ones, since an in-app tip goes straight to them.
 Holiday Tips 2026 : Mail, Packages, And Delivery Who Suggested Tip Or Gift Good To Know 
 USPS Mail Carrier Gift worth $20 or less, no cash or cash-like gift cards Federal rules cap gifts at $50 a year per customer. 
 UPS Driver Gift or treats, about $20 Drivers are told to decline cash. 
 FedEx Driver Gift under $75, no cash or gift cards The $75 limit is per year. 
 Amazon Delivery Driver Thank My Driver, or snacks on the porch Amazon paid drivers $5 per thank-you in 2025. 
 Newspaper Carrier $10 to $30 Some papers add a tip envelope in December. 
 Grocery Delivery Shopper (Regular) $10 to $20 extra in the app Tip in the app so the shopper gets it. 
 Food Delivery Driver (Regular) $5 to $10 extra on a December order Only if the same driver comes often. 
 Water Or Propane Delivery $15 to $25, or treats Regular routes only. 
 Source: The College Investor, Emily Post Institute, Bankrate. Personal Care, Beauty, And Fitness
 Personal care is where the “cost of one visit” rule fits best. Most of these workers are in jobs on the Treasury’s list of jobs eligible for the no tax on tips deduction , so your tip may qualify for that deduction on their return.
 Holiday Tips 2026 : Personal Care, Beauty, And Fitness Who Suggested Tip Or Gift Good To Know 
 Hairstylist Or Colorist Cost of one visit, or a gift Salon owners are optional. 
 Barber Cost of one cut Regulars only. 
 Nail Technician Cost of one visit Split it if more than one tech helps you. 
 Esthetician Or Facialist Cost of one visit, or a gift Monthly clients and up. 
 Massage Therapist Cost of one session, or a gift Clinic therapists may not accept cash. 
 Lash Or Brow Technician Cost of one visit Regular fills only. 
 Personal Trainer Cost of one session, or a gift Gym policies vary, so ask first. 
 Fitness Instructor Small gift or card, $10 to $20 For a class you attend every week. 
 Source: The College Investor, Emily Post Institute, Bankrate. Pets
 Pet care is personal, and a walker or sitter who sees your animals every week earns a bigger thank-you than an occasional groomer. Many dog walkers book through apps like Rover , so you can add a holiday tip right in the app.
 Holiday Tips 2026 : Pets Who Suggested Tip Or Gift Good To Know 
 Dog Walker One week’s pay Daily walkers rank near the top. 
 Pet Sitter Cost of one visit, or a gift Give more if they cover your holiday travel. 
 Dog Groomer Cost of one session Regular grooming only. 
 Dog Trainer Gift, or $20 to $40 Only for ongoing training. 
 Boarding Or Doggy Daycare Staff Treats or a group gift, $20 to $50 Drop it off for the whole team. 
 Veterinarian Treats for the office, no cash Vets are professionals, not tipped staff. 
 Source: The College Investor, Emily Post Institute, Bankrate. Healthcare And Eldercare
 Agencies, hospitals, and care homes often bar staff from taking cash, so ask before you give. A donation can stand in for a tip, and a gift to a qualified nonprofit can count as a charitable contribution on your taxes.
 Holiday Tips 2026 : Healthcare And Eldercare Who Suggested Tip Or Gift Good To Know 
 Home Health Aide (Agency) Gift, if the agency allows it Many agencies ban cash. 
 Private Caregiver Or Companion One week’s pay, or a gift Treat a full-time caregiver like a nanny. 
 Nursing Home Or Assisted Living Staff Group gift for the floor, like a food tray Facilities often ban individual tips. 
 Private Duty Nurse One week’s pay, or a gift Agency nurses may be limited. 
 Hospice Team Donation to the organization, plus a card A note naming staff means a lot. 
 Doctor, Dentist, Or Therapist Treats for the office, no tip Professionals don’t expect a tip. 
 Source: The College Investor, Emily Post Institute, Bankrate. Regulars Around Town
 Your regulars around town are optional, but a December thank-you builds goodwill. If you tip on a card, a cash back credit card returns a little of it, as long as you pay the balance in full.
 Holiday Tips 2026 : Regulars Around Town Who Suggested Tip Or Gift Good To Know 
 Regular Barista $10 to $25 Or a bigger tip on one December visit. 
 Regular Bartender Or Server $20 to $50 For a spot you visit every week. 
 Valet At Work Or Home $20 to $50 Daily users only. 
 Car Wash Attendant (Membership) $10 to $20 Leave it with the crew lead. 
 Tailor Or Shoe Repair $10 to $20, or treats Frequent customers only. 
 Regular Rideshare Or Car Service Driver $20 to $50 For a driver you book directly. 
 Source: The College Investor, Emily Post Institute, Bankrate. Work And Business
 Work tips and gifts come with tax rules, especially if you own the business. Business owners should handle client gifts and staff bonuses as part of their year-end business checklist .
 Holiday Tips 2026 : Work And Business Who Suggested Tip Or Gift Good To Know 
 Office Cleaning Crew $20 to $40 each, or treats Night crews are easy to forget. 
 Administrative Assistant Gift worth $25 to $100 From you personally, not the company. 
 Mailroom Or Front Desk Staff $10 to $20, or treats A group gift from your team works. 
 Your Boss No gift, or a group card Gifts usually flow down, not up. 
 Your Employees Cash bonus or gift Cash and gift cards count as taxable wages. 
 Clients Gift Only $25 per client per year is deductible. 
 Source: The College Investor, Emily Post Institute, Bankrate. Public Workers
 Many city, state, and federal workers can’t accept cash at all. When the rules say no, a card or a donation in their name is the safe choice, and none of it touches the gift tax at these amounts.
 Holiday Tips 2026 : Public Workers Who Suggested Tip Or Gift Good To Know 
 Trash And Recycling Crew (Private Hauler) $10 to $30 per worker Bankrate’s 2025 median was $25. 
 Trash And Recycling Crew (City Workers) A card, check city rules NYC and Philadelphia ban tips, even small treats. 
 Crossing Guard A card, or treats if allowed Often a city or school employee. 
 Police And Firefighters Donation to a station fund, or a card Individual officers shouldn’t take cash. 
 Federal Employees Gift worth $20 or less, no cash The same rule that covers USPS carriers. 
 Source: The College Investor, Emily Post Institute, Bankrate. Holiday Tip Planner: Add Up Your List
 Check off everyone you plan to thank, edit the amounts to match what you pay, and the planner totals your list. Enter a budget and press Fit To My Budget to scale every amount down to your number, then copy the list into your notes or a budgeting app .
 Holiday Tip Planner 2026 $0 Your Tip Total 0 People Thanked — Set A Budget My Budget Fit To My Budget Copy My List Reset Check who you plan to thank, then edit amounts to match what you actually pay. Defaults are The College Investor’s suggested starting points. Who Can’t Accept Cash Tips?
 USPS mail carriers, other federal employees, many city workers, and some public school teachers face legal limits on gifts. Several delivery companies also bar drivers from taking cash. A small non-cash gift and a card is the safe move for these workers, and store cards from discount gift card sites stretch your budget.
 Who Can’t Take Cash: 2026 Gift Rules Who The Rule Cash? Give Instead 
 USPS Mail Carriers Gifts up to $20 per occasion and $50 a year per customer. No cash, checks, or cash-like gift cards. No Cash Snacks, a $20 coffee shop card, warm gloves 
 Other Federal Employees Same $20 and $50 limits under federal ethics rules. No Cash A card or a small treat 
 City Workers In NYC And Philadelphia Tips of any value are banned for city employees doing their jobs. No Tips A thank-you note or a call to the department 
 Public School Teachers Depends on state and district. Massachusetts allows class gifts up to $150 a year. Check Rules A class gift or classroom supplies 
 UPS Drivers No published customer policy. Drivers are told to decline cash. Gifts Okay Snacks, drinks, or a small gift 
 FedEx Drivers No cash or gift cards. Gifts up to $75 a year. Gifts Okay Snacks or a small gift 
 Amazon Drivers No published tip limit. Holiday Thank My Driver promotions have paid $5 per thank-you. Use The App Thank My Driver, or a porch snack bin 
 Agency Caregivers And Care Homes Set by the agency or facility. Many ban cash. Check Rules A group food tray or a donation 
 Source: 5 CFR 2635.204, NYC Conflicts Of Interest Board, City Of Philadelphia, Massachusetts State Ethics Commission, Amazon. The College Investor. USPS Mail Carrier Gift Rules
 Postal workers follow the same federal ethics rule as other executive branch employees. A carrier can accept a gift worth $20 or less per occasion, up to $50 a year from one customer. Cash, checks, and Visa or Mastercard gift cards are off limits in any amount. A $20 coffee shop or restaurant card is fine, and you can often buy one below face value through gift card resale sites .
 UPS, FedEx, And Amazon Driver Rules
 FedEx drivers can’t take cash or gift cards, but they can accept gifts worth up to $75 a year. UPS drivers are told to decline cash, McClatchy News reported , so snacks or a small gift work better. Amazon’s Thank My Driver promotion paid drivers $5 per thank-you in December 2025, at no cost to customers. Gig drivers on food delivery apps get tips in the app instead.
 City Workers And Public School Teachers
 New York City’s Conflicts of Interest Board (PDF File) says public servants may not take a tip of any value for doing their jobs. Philadelphia (PDF File) tells its sanitation crews to turn down cash tips from residents. A donation to a local food bank in the crew’s name breaks no rules, and it can count as a charitable contribution .
 Teacher rules vary by state. The Massachusetts State Ethics Commission allows a class gift of up to $150 per school year, plus individual gifts under $50 from families who didn’t chip in. A pooled class gift card is the easiest way to stay inside limits like these, and you can buy one at a discount through discount gift card sites .
 How Much Do Americans Actually Tip At The Holidays?
 Fewer people planned holiday tips in 2025, but those who tipped gave about the same as before. The share planning to tip fell for every provider in Bankrate’s 2025 survey . Childcare saw the biggest drop, from 55% to 47%, and tight budgets show up elsewhere too, with credit card debt at $1.18 trillion in 2025.
 How Americans Tipped In 2025 Provider Plan To Tip 2025 Plan To Tip 2024 Median Tip 2025 Median Tip 2024 
 House Cleaner 56% 57% $50 $50 
 Childcare Provider 47% 55% $48 $50 
 Teacher 47% 53% $25 $25 
 Lawn, Garden, Or Snow Crew 37% 41% $50 $30 
 Mail Carrier 27% 31% $20 $20 
 Trash And Recycling Collector 21% 26% $25 $20 
 Source: Bankrate Holiday Tipping Survey, 2025. Share is among people who use each service. The College Investor. Median tips held at $50 for house cleaners, $25 for teachers, and $20 for mail carriers, while lawn and snow crews jumped from $30 to $50. Younger adults feel the most pressure, and Bankrate found 44% of Gen Z and 42% of millennials feel obligated to tip. If that pressure stresses you out, a short no-buy challenge in November can free up cash for the people who matter most.
 How To Tip On A Tight Budget
 Start with the people you see most, like your sitter and house cleaner. Then cut amounts in half before you cut anyone from the list, and use cards, homemade treats, and group gifts for the rest. Plan the total the same way you’d build any budget , with a number first and names second.
 A Sample Tip List At Two Budgets
 A typical suburban family with a biweekly cleaner, a sitter, two school-age kids, a dog walker, and a lawn crew can easily spend $585 following full etiquette. The tight budget version below thanks every person on that list for $275, a 53% cut. Run your own numbers in the planner above, then track them in a budgeting app .
 Sample Holiday Tip List: $585 Vs. $275 Who Full Etiquette Amount Tight Budget Version 
 Biweekly House Cleaner $160 (one visit) $80 plus a card 
 Regular Babysitter $80 (one night) $40 plus a kid-made card 
 Two K-12 Teachers $50 $20 toward two class gifts 
 USPS Mail Carrier $20 gift Homemade cookies 
 Trash Crew, Two Workers (Private Hauler) $40 $20 
 Hairstylist $75 (one visit) $35 
 Dog Walker $100 (one week) $50 
 Lawn Crew, Two Workers $60 $30 
 Total $585 $275 
 Source: The College Investor sample household. Amounts are illustrative. Pay For Holiday Tips Without Debt
 Set aside a small amount each month in a separate savings bucket, and December tips stop feeling like a surprise. Pulling the cash out ahead of time works like the envelope challenge , since you can only hand out what’s in the envelope.
 Skip pay-later apps for tips and gifts, because buy now, pay later plans can now affect your credit score . If holiday spending already sits on a card you can’t pay off, look at legitimate credit card debt relief before adding more.
 Holiday Tipping For College Students
 College students on a tight budget can skip cash entirely. A signed card for the dining hall crew or a group gift from your floor for the building custodian goes a long way. Our ways to save money in college can help you find room for small gifts.
 Many students sit on the other side of the tip jar, too. Babysitting, dog walking, and delivery all show up on our list of side hustles for college students , and holiday tips can make December one of the better months for those jobs.
 Cash, Gift Card, Or Gift: What Should You Give?
 Cash is the best tip for most service workers, because it’s flexible and arrives right when holiday bills hit. Give a store-specific gift card to workers who can’t take cash, and give a gift to professionals and teachers. Crisp bills in a card with a handwritten note beat cash handed over at the door, and store cards from discount gift card sites stretch your money.
 Payment apps are fine for nannies, sitters, and dog walkers you already pay that way. Send the tip from your personal account with a note so it reads as a holiday thank-you. Our comparison of Cash App, Venmo, Zelle, and PayPal can help if you’re choosing one. Workers paid through a business profile may see those payments on a Form 1099-K .
 Gift Ideas Within The USPS Limit
 A $20 coffee or restaurant card, a box of baked goods, warm gloves, or a reusable water bottle all fit the USPS limit and most delivery company policies. For city workers who can’t accept anything, a thank-you note to their department gets noticed.
 When Should You Give Holiday Tips?
 Give holiday tips in the first two weeks of December, or at the last visit before the holiday. Tipping early means workers have the money for their own holiday spending. Buying gift cards and small gifts during Black Friday and Cyber Monday sales helps your budget too.
 For crews you never see, like trash collectors, hand the envelope over in person or tape a clearly labeled card to the bin the morning of pickup. Missed the window? A New Year’s card with a tip is still welcome, and a tip in January beats skipping it.
 Are Holiday Tips And Gifts Taxable?
 For most givers, holiday tips aren’t deductible and won’t trigger any tax. Household employers and business owners are the exceptions. Personal gifts stay well under the $19,000 annual gift tax exclusion for 2026 , so there’s no paperwork for the giver. The workers who receive tips owe income tax on them.
 Holiday Bonuses For A Nanny Or Housekeeper
 A cash holiday bonus to a household employee counts as cash wages under IRS Publication 926 . For 2026, Social Security and Medicare taxes apply once you pay one household employee $3,000 or more in cash wages. Once you cross that line, the bonus counts toward the wages you report on their Form W-2 , while non-cash gifts like a sweater or a meal don’t count as cash wages.
 Holiday Gifts From A Business
 A business can deduct only $25 per client per year for gifts under IRS Publication 463 . Cash and gift cards to employees count as taxable wages under IRS Publication 15-B , no matter the amount. Run both through payroll and your books as part of your year-end business checklist .
 For Workers Who Receive Holiday Tips
 Tips are taxable income, but the new no tax on tips deduction lets eligible workers deduct up to $25,000 in qualified tips for 2025 through 2028. Nannies, babysitters, house cleaners, pet sitters, hairstylists, trainers, and delivery workers are among the jobs eligible for the deduction , which phases out above $150,000 of income for single filers and $300,000 for joint filers.
 A voluntary holiday tip from a customer may count as a qualified tip, while a bonus your employer pays through payroll is wages, not a tip. Self-employed workers still owe self-employment tax on tip income, so check with a tax pro before you claim it.
 What To Write In A Holiday Tip Card
 Keep the note short, name something specific they did this year, and sign it from the whole household. A specific line means more than a long one, and kids can sign the card or chip in from their own debit card for kids . Here are lines you can borrow.
 “Thank you for keeping our home running all year. We notice every detail, and we’re grateful.” For A House Cleaner “The kids talk about you all week. Thank you for being someone they trust.” For A Nanny Or Sitter “Rain, snow, and a mountain of packages, and you never missed a day. Happy holidays.” For A Mail Carrier “Thank you for everything you did for our family this year. Enjoy a coffee on us.” For A Teacher “Our dog thinks you hung the moon. So do we.” For A Dog Walker If you can’t give a tip this year, the card on its own is still a real thank-you. Pair it with homemade treats. Save your cash for people you pay directly, like a dog walker you booked through Rover .
 Frequently Asked Questions
 Should I Tip My Mail Carrier For Christmas?
 You can’t give a USPS carrier cash or a cash-like gift card. You can give a gift worth $20 or less, like snacks or a coffee shop card, up to $50 a year from one customer. Store cards are easy to find through discount gift card sites .
 How Much Do You Tip A House Cleaner For The Holidays?
 The standard is the cost of one visit for a weekly or biweekly cleaner. Bankrate’s 2025 survey found a median holiday tip of $50, so many people give less than a full visit. Half a visit plus a card is fine on a tight budget .
 Is It Rude Not To Tip For The Holidays?
 No. Holiday tips are a thank-you, not a bill, and a handwritten card is a real gesture when money is tight. If you tip every visit year-round, a smaller holiday tip or card is plenty. Your emergency fund should come first.
 Do You Tip Teachers For The Holidays?
 Teachers usually get a gift or gift card, not cash. Bankrate found a $25 median in 2025, and some states cap gifts to public school teachers. A class gift from several families often works best, and discount gift card sites stretch the pool.
 How Much Should I Give My Nanny For Christmas?
 One week’s pay is standard for a full-time nanny, often with a small gift from your child. A cash bonus counts as wages for household payroll taxes, so add it to the nanny’s Form W-2 total.
 Do You Tip Your Trash Collector At Christmas?
 Many people give $10 to $30 per worker, and Bankrate’s 2025 median was $25. City sanitation workers in places like New York City and Philadelphia can’t accept tips, so check whether your hauler is public or private first.
 Can I Tip My Amazon Or UPS Driver?
 Amazon’s Thank My Driver promotion paid drivers $5 per thank-you during the 2025 holidays, at no cost to customers. UPS drivers are told to decline cash, so snacks or a small gift work better. App-based drivers on Uber Eats can get tips right in the app.
 What Can I Give Instead Of A Cash Tip?
 Store gift cards, baked goods, warm accessories, or a handwritten card all work. For care homes and agencies that ban cash, a group food tray is the safe choice. A donation to the organization works too, and it can count as a charitable contribution .
